ety.text: Borrowed from Marathi -च (-ċ), from Old Marathi -𑘓 (-ca), -𑘓𑘲 (-cī), from Maharastri Prakrit 𑀘𑀺𑀅 (cia), from Ashokan Prakrit 𑀘𑁂𑀯 (ceva), from Sanskrit चैव (caiva), from च (ca) + एव (evá).

x: मैं उससे अक्सर हिन्दी बोलता हूँ।

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian اَکْثَر (aksar), from Arabic أَكْثَر (ʔakṯar). Compare Bengali আকসার (akśar).

s.g: the fiftieth year of Jupiter's cycle
alternative spelling of अनैच्छिक मांसपेशी (anaicchik mānspeśī)
happy! how happy! blessed! how fortunate! joy
exclamation of praise and wonder; hail! bravo!

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian خْوَشَا (xwašā), from خْوَش (xwaš, “happy”), whence Hindi ख़ुश (xuś).

s.g: alternative spelling of गज़ (gaz): gudge: a historic unit of length equivalent to sixteen girah, redefined under British occupation as exactly equal to a yard

ety.text: From some variant of Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀘𑀁𑀘𑀼 (caṃcu, “beak”), borrowed from Dravidian. Compare Tamil சொண்டு (coṇṭu).

x: पुराने भवन की जर्जरता को देखकर उसे खाली कर दिया गया।

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit जर्जरता (jarjaratā). By surface analysis, जर्जर (jarjar) + -ता (-tā).
Inherited from Sanskrit *आत्रिश्वस् (*ātriśvas). Cognate with Marathi तेरवा (tervā).

s.g: a type of open palanquin or sedan chair

ety.text: Inherited from Sanskrit *तिथि-वार (*tithi-vāra) and older Hindi तेवहार (tevhār); cognate with Gujarati તહેવાર (tahevār).

s.g: to cause to run, impel to run; to urge on

इतिहास यह भी बताता है कि जिन-जिन राष्ट्रों ने अनुकरण द्वारा आधुनिक बनने का रास्ता अपनाया है और अपनी भाषा-नीति के माध्यम से एक नकलची बुद्धिजीवी वर्ग को पैदा किया है, वहीं आधुनिकता के नाम पर मानसिक गुलामी आयी है।

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian مازو (māzū, “gallnut”) + फल (phal, “fruit”). Compare मायाफल (māyāphal) (a Sanskrit borrowing) and माईफल (māīphal) (a direct descendant from Proto-Indo-Aryan).

s.g: many successive epochs, a very long period of time

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit विभाजन (vibhājana). By surface analysis, वि- (vi-) + भाजन (bhājan).

x: आप बैठिए, मैं उसे पूरी बात समझाऊँगा।

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian حرامزاده (harām-zāda). Equivalent to हराम (harām, “illicit, illegitimate”) + -ज़ादा (-zādā, “child, offspring”). Cognate with Bengali হারামজাদা (haramjada).

s.g: an exclamation of distress, affliction or fear; alas

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀳𑀸 (hā), from Sanskrit हा (hā), ultimately of onomatopoeic origin.

s.g: sound of distress, affliction, or fear
